newsitem.title: PERU: Fujimori makes first speech to nation since crisis.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori makes first speech to nation since crisis.

text.p: The following is a complete translation of President Alberto Fujimori's speech to the nation on Saturday, his first since Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels took over the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima on Tuesday.

"For four days, as we all know, hundreds of Peruvians and foreigners have been held, as hostages, in the Japanese ambassador's residence, in what constitutes a repugnant attack against the freedom, health and life of innocent people.

"Although it seems incredible, with this act of terror and flagrant violation of human rights, the so-called MRTA, the same that in the last decade was sowing destruction and death in Peru, and whose best-known representatives are Victor Polay Campos, Peter Cardenas Schultz, Lucero Cumpa among others, hopes to start a dialogue that leads to a peace accord. That is to say, they hope for dialogue by placing an AKM rifle on the neck of hostages.
"My government is not prepared to accept that the force and violence of a terrorist command can be imposed on 23 million people, who reject these methods, which are neither civilized or political.
"We cannot talk of peace or accord while terror is used as the main argument.
"From the beginning of these lamentable events, the government put in place an emergency strategy, which it did not publicize for obvious reasons, with the objective of avoiding bloodshed.

"In the context of this strategy, my government has not planned solutions of force, for which reason it has not rejected dialogue, this being shown by the appointment of (Education) Minister Domingo Paleremo as its spokesman. Our spokesman, with the mediation of the Red Cross' representative, achieved the freedom of 38 hostages.
"It is, above all, clear that the freedom of those who perpetrated murders and terrorist attacks is unacceptable in the framework of Peru's current laws and by the criteria of national security.

"However, my government does not avoid its responsibility in the search for a way out, and has the clearest will to act with human feeling and to secure that this problem is overcome by pacific means, that is to say, achieving a way out that does not violate the human rights either of the hostages or the captors.

"The proposal is concrete. That the captors lay down the weapons to a guarantor committee and that they allow the evacuation of all the hostages without exception. In this way, the possibility of the use of force by the Peruvian state will be ruled out and from there, with all guarantees, a way out can be studied.
"This is the proposal of the government before the country and the international community. And I can only hope for an outcome that reflects the sense of respect for the life of innocent people."
